title: refactor(ci): modernize and unify lint/test/release workflows
author: Marin Patel
description: Motivation: Our repo accumulated many ad-hoc GitHub Actions and duplicated matrices across services. This PR consolidates lint/test/release pipelines into a shared, opinionated set of workflows and helper actions to reduce flakiness, improve caching, and make release automation consistent across packages. Goals: 1) unify lint/test matrices (node versions, OSes, python) into a reusable composite workflow; 2) centralize cache and build helpers to reduce CI runtime and cache miss rate; 3) modernize release automation to use the new release orchestration action with clearer cutover steps; 4) remove legacy per-repo scripts that diverge from the organization standard. What changed (high level): - Added .github/workflows/ci-unified.yml: composite/invoker pattern to run lint + unit/integration tests across repos with per-package overrides. - Replaced many repo-specific workflows with a thin invoker that calls into the unified workflow. - Introduced .github/actions/cache-helpers to standardize restore/save logic (keys, compression, partial restores). - Updated release workflow to use actions/release-orchestrator v2 with explicit canary and stable phases, and safer tag-and-publish steps. - Consolidated node/pip matrices and dropped unsupported Node 14 entries. - Small updates to SDK build scripts to be compatible with the new matrix (npm ci -> npm ci --prefer-offline where appropriate). Backwards compatibility and migration: invoker workflows are feature-flagged by a repository-level config in .github/ci-config.yml; default rollout enabled for monorepo packages. For Dedicated/private installers we keep the previous release job as a fallback for one release cycle (see rollout instructions). Checklist: - [x] consolidated lint/test matrices - [x] cache helpers implemented and unit-tested - [x] release workflow updated with canary/stable phases - [x] migration docs added in tools/ci/README.md - [x] rollout gated by .github/ci-config.yml - [x] smoke-tested on redwood-examples and redwood-sdk-* How to roll back: revert the invoker workflow or update .github/ci-config.yml to disable unified mode; legacy workflows are retained for a single release cycle to allow rollback. Related: ENG-7890 (CI consolidation), ENG-8120 (release automation modernize).

docs(ci): add rollout & rollback steps to tools/ci/README.md

review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice consolidation — can you add a note about cache key collisions when multiple workspaces restore the same key?
Author (Marin Patel): Added deterministic scope to keys in cache-helpers (package name + hash) to avoid collisions.
Diego Morales: The release job looks safer but we should ensure we don't auto-promote canary tags if there are open regressions. Consider gating on 'quality:ok' artifact.
Author: Added explicit artifact check and a manual approval step before stable promotion; documented behavior in README.
Lena Fischer: CI times improved locally — did you measure percent improvement org-wide?
Author: Initial numbers: median CI runtime for lint+unit fell ~28% across sampled packages; added a short section in README with methodology and raw numbers.
Samir Rao: Minor nit: update team-oncall workflow to reference new cache helper action
Author: Updated team-oncall invoker to use cache-helpers and pinned action version v1.0.0
ci_reruns: 2026-02-18: reran matrix after cache key fix (previously some jobs had cold cache)
2026-02-20: reran release dry-run after adding manual approval step
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows: unified lint/test matrices, improved cache helpers, modernized release orchestration (canary+stable), reduced CI median runtime (~28% on sampled packages). Rollout: enabled by default; follow tools/ci/README.md for migration and rollback.
notes_for_release: This is a CI/tooling only change — no runtime user-facing behavior expected.
Teams: update local CI debug docs if you rely on legacy workflows.
If any repo sees unexpected failures, set .github/ci-config.yml -> unified_mode: false to opt-out and open ENG-7890 for tracking.
notes: Merged after approvals from core infra reviewers; retained legacy workflows for one release cycle to allow opt-out.
